coordination.title: Coordination and referral
coordination.summary: Prepare a state-law path early when the facts suggest one. Congress retains its own work and the receiving office makes its own decision.
facts: Who starts
Committee counsel screens for a possible state-law issue and identifies which office could act.
What can move now
Authorized contacts may discuss jurisdiction and handling procedures without transmitting protected evidence.
choices: coordination-screen
Identify a plausible state statute and a factual link to the state before treating an office as a possible recipient.
coordination-handling
Draft a handling plan in advance. Use placeholders until the recipient and scope are verified.
congressional-action
Keep the congressional track moving even if a state-law basis is unavailable or the recipient declines.

coordination-screen.title: Screen jurisdiction
coordination-screen.summary: Check the statute, its elements, the facts connecting the conduct to the state, venue, timing and the receiving office’s authority.
facts: Working record
Record the proposed law, fact-to-element match, open questions, responsible counsel and any special appointment or referral required.
choices: coordination-new-york
Use this New York example if the facts support a New York issue. Confirm the law and office on the specific matter.
coordination-washington
Use this Washington example if the facts support a Washington issue. Confirm the law and office on the specific matter.
coordination-other-state
Use the jurisdiction checklist and official directories for a state without a worked example.
coordination-no-recipient
Pause the state pathway when a statute, factual connection, venue or office authority is missing.

coordination-other-state.title: Check another state
coordination-other-state.summary: The map includes worked examples for New York and Washington. For another jurisdiction, counsel must verify which law and office apply before routing evidence.
facts: Attorney general
Find the serving office in the official directory and verify the specific statute or appointment under which it could act.
Local prosecutor
Check the relevant county, venue and any special assignments under state law.
Regulator
Check the activity, charter or license and the agency's enforcement authority.
No established recipient
Record the missing legal or factual basis and hold the referral while congressional work continues.
choices: coordination-contacts
Once an office's authority is verified, identify the authorized contact and confirm the secure channel.
coordination-no-recipient
Hold the proposed referral when office authority or jurisdiction is unresolved.

coordination-new-york.title: New York
coordination-new-york.summary: Select the office type after checking the applicable New York statute and the facts. The presence of an account in New York alone supplies no decision about a referral.
choices: coordination-ny-ag
Check a specific statutory grant or a valid executive or agency referral before identifying the Attorney General as a criminal recipient.
coordination-ny-prosecutor
For a state crime, check the county’s venue and any special prosecutorial assignment.
coordination-ny-regulator
Check whether the activity and entity fall within the Department of Financial Services’ supervisory authority.
coordination-no-recipient
Record no established recipient when no jurisdictional or agency basis can be confirmed.

coordination-ny-ag.title: New York Attorney General
coordination-ny-ag.summary: Executive Law § 63 provides different authorities for different matters. Section 63(12) provides a civil path for repeated fraudulent or illegal acts or persistent fraud or illegality in business. Sections 63(2) and (3) describe distinct criminal referral routes.
choices: coordination-contacts
Verify which subdivision or other statute applies and which unit is authorized for this matter.

coordination-ny-prosecutor.title: New York district attorney
coordination-ny-prosecutor.summary: County Law § 700 sets out a district attorney’s duties for crimes cognizable by the county courts, subject to exceptions. Counsel checks venue and any special assignment.
choices: coordination-contacts
Verify the competent county office through its official channel before discussing a proposed transfer.

coordination-ny-regulator.title: New York financial regulator
coordination-ny-regulator.summary: The Department of Financial Services supervises covered financial entities and activities. Verify the entity’s license or charter and the governing regulatory provision.
choices: coordination-contacts
Confirm that the agency supervises this entity and activity, and verify its official contact for the matter.

coordination-washington.title: Washington
coordination-washington.summary: Select the office type after checking the Washington statute and facts. Criminal prosecution and financial supervision have separate authorities.
choices: coordination-wa-ag
Check whether the statutory process for an Attorney General prosecution applies.
coordination-wa-prosecutor
Check the county prosecutor’s authority and venue for the conduct at issue.
coordination-wa-regulator
Check the institution’s charter, license and regulated activity before routing to DFI.
coordination-no-recipient
Record no established recipient if no state-law or agency basis can be confirmed.

coordination-wa-ag.title: Washington Attorney General
coordination-wa-ag.summary: RCW 43.10.232 grants concurrent authority upon a qualifying written request or concurrence. The relevant county prosecutor, the governor or a majority of the organized crime oversight committee can supply it.
facts: Before prosecution
The Attorney General and the county must reach an agreement on payment of prosecution costs under this section.
choices: coordination-contacts
Confirm any necessary request or concurrence and the authorized unit before treating this office as a recipient.

coordination-wa-prosecutor.title: Washington county prosecutor
coordination-wa-prosecutor.summary: RCW 36.27.020 assigns prosecutorial duties to county prosecutors. Confirm the relevant county and any statutory allocation or exception for the matter.
choices: coordination-contacts
Verify the competent county office through its official channel before discussing a proposed transfer.

coordination-wa-regulator.title: Washington financial regulator
coordination-wa-regulator.summary: The Department of Financial Institutions supervises covered providers, including Washington state-chartered banks and certain licensed money transmitters. Charter or license helps identify the correct regulator.
choices: coordination-contacts
Confirm the entity and activity are within the agency’s authority, and verify the appropriate unit.

coordination-no-recipient.title: No established recipient
coordination-no-recipient.summary: Hold the state referral. Record the missing fact, legal basis or authority and the condition for reconsidering the decision.
choices: congressional-action
Take any supported legislative action within the committee’s own authority.

coordination-contacts.title: Verify authorized contacts
coordination-contacts.summary: Verify the office, authorized contact and secure intake channel independently. Discuss process at first and obtain agreement before any case material moves.
facts: Who can act
Authorized congressional staff and the verified receiving office contact. Each side confirms its authority and capacity.
What is missing
A case-specific recipient and the materials each side is authorized to receive, use or retain.
choices: coordination-handling
With both offices identified, record which channels and handling rules each office approves.

coordination-handling.title: Agree on handling procedures
coordination-handling.summary: Document ownership, permitted uses, access, security, retention, corrections, witness issues and independent decision-making before any transfer.
facts: Authority
A handling agreement sets procedures. Each disclosure still requires its own legal basis and approval.
Record
Name the sending and receiving custodians, correction contacts, secure channel and how access is reviewed.
choices: coordination-disclosure
Only when the recipient and procedure are verified may counsel assess each item for possible disclosure.
witness-restricted
If a record could be restricted by immunity, privilege or safety concerns, route it to authorized counsel for review.

coordination-disclosure.title: Approve each disclosure
coordination-disclosure.summary: Identify the exact materials, authority to disclose, restrictions, required redactions and authorized committee decision. Use the verified secure channel.
facts: Approval
Counsel checks privilege, immunity, privacy and other restrictions. The authorized official records what may move, to whom and for which purpose.
Hold condition
Keep protected or unapproved items in their authorized system. Reassess a narrower disclosure if the packet cannot proceed.
choices: coordination-disposition
Send only the approved version after documenting state-law basis, authorized recipient, disclosures and transfer channel.
coordination-hold-disclosure
Hold the referral if disclosure approval or secure transfer remains unresolved, even if the receiving office is known.

coordination-hold-disclosure.title: Hold the disclosure
coordination-hold-disclosure.summary: Record which item, approval or transfer condition is unresolved. Preserve the existing authorization and record restrictions while counsel reviews options.
choices: coordination-disclosure
Reassess an authorized redaction, narrower packet or verified secure channel only if counsel identifies a lawful option.

coordination-disposition.title: Referral and disposition
coordination-disposition.summary: Track approval, delivery and any confirmed disposition separately. The receiving office may decline, investigate or pursue a remedy under its own law.
facts: What delivery establishes
A receipt confirms delivery. Record further action only when the office confirms it and disclosure of the status is authorized.
What happens next
Assign an authorized follow-up owner and a review date. Preserve a correction and version history.
choices: congressional-action
Congress continues its separately authorized response without depending on a state enforcement decision.

witnesses.title: Witness cooperation and immunity
witnesses.summary: Seek complete, truthful information and corroborate it. Keep voluntary cooperation, compelled testimony under an immunity order and clemency separate.
choices: witness-voluntary
Identify the authorized interviewer or prosecutor and confirm the witness’s voluntary participation or the agreement’s legal authority.
witness-compelled
If the witness invokes the privilege against self-incrimination, counsel checks the statutory procedure and its risks before seeking an order.
witness-clemency
Only the legally empowered authority can decide whether to grant clemency.
witness-restricted
Apply the record-specific limits before access, further review or any transfer.

witness-voluntary.title: Voluntary or negotiated cooperation
witness-voluntary.summary: Authorized congressional staff may request a voluntary interview. A prosecutor with jurisdiction may negotiate within that office’s authority and any required approvals.
facts: Terms
Identify the covered conduct, parties, duties, consequences for false statements and any office outside the agreement’s scope.
Evidence
Seek a truthful account regardless of whether it supports the hypothesis. Corroborate important details with independent records or testimony.
choices: witness-restricted
Confirm permitted uses and who may review the interview and agreement before sharing either.

witness-compelled.title: Compelled congressional testimony
witness-compelled.summary: Under 18 U.S.C. §§ 6002 and 6005, a duly authorized congressional representative requests a federal district court order when the witness refuses on self-incrimination grounds.
facts: Approval
For a chamber proceeding, a majority of members present must approve. For a committee or subcommittee proceeding, two-thirds of the members of the full committee must approve.
Notice and court order

Serve the U.S. attorney general at least 10 days before requesting the order. On the attorney general’s application the court must defer issuance for the specified period, up to 20 days from the request. The presiding officer communicates the order to the witness.
choices: witness-independent
Decide how to isolate compelled material and demonstrate independent provenance before an authorized prosecution team sees evidence.

witness-independent.title: Independent evidence sources
witness-independent.summary: The compelled information and what derives from it generally cannot be used against that witness in a criminal case. The statute has limited exceptions for perjury, false statements and noncompliance.
facts: Burden
Under Kastigar, the prosecution must demonstrate a legitimate independent source for evidence it proposes to use once the immunity issue is raised as required.
Proposed safeguard
Keep compelled testimony and its leads separate. Track how and when the independent team obtained each item and record any exposure for counsel review.
choices: witness-restricted
Apply role-based access and keep an exposure log before anyone opens a record or follows a lead.

witness-clemency.title: Pardon or commutation
witness-clemency.summary: Clemency is a separate decision by the legally empowered authority. Check the jurisdiction, covered conduct and terms of the grant.
facts: Federal
The President’s pardon power covers offenses against the United States. State-law offenses fall under state clemency authority.
State example
In Washington the governor holds clemency powers under state law and the board makes recommendations. Check the applicable state’s own constitution and statutes.
choices: lessons-clemency
Review the historical proclamation and its actual scope before drawing conclusions about another matter.

witness-restricted.title: Restricted records and access
witness-restricted.summary: In an authorized workspace, show each record’s restrictions and permitted roles. A blocked team sees the reason and an approved review route without receiving protected contents.
facts: Proposed access model
Separate private collection, counsel review and authorized publication. Keep compelled material, derived leads, independent sources and exposure histories separately controlled.
Public map
Only public material and fictional examples belong here. Secure record handling and real permissions live in the authorized institution’s own systems.
choices: review
Return to evidence review with only the material this team may access.
coordination-disclosure
Review any proposed external disclosure item by item through authorized counsel.

lessons.title: January 6 lessons and failure points
lessons.summary: Follow the public record from collection and contested requests through referrals, federal prosecutions and clemency. Each screen separates the historical record from a proposed safeguard.
choices: lessons-preservation
Start with the documented public record and its custody.
lessons-delay
Check how authorization and decision dates constrain the work.
lessons-contested
Examine the documented privilege dispute and its outcome.
lessons-witnesses
Separate witness testimony, corroboration and lawful limits.
lessons-referrals
Distinguish committee referrals from prosecutorial decisions.
lessons-prosecutions
Use dated charging and court records to evaluate outcomes.
lessons-clemency
Read the proclamation to determine who and what it covered.

lessons-preservation.title: Evidence preservation
lessons-preservation.summary: The House Select Committee published its final report and released hearing and supporting materials. GovInfo preserves a collection of those public records.
facts: Proposed safeguard
Assign custody at the outset and record source, date, original format and access limits. Maintain an approved publication copy and a separate preservation record.
choices: lessons-delay
Check preservation and authorized milestones before setting investigative deadlines.

lessons-delay.title: Delay and deadlines
lessons-delay.summary: The House established the Select Committee on June 30, 2021. Its final report is dated December 22, 2022. Requests and disputes had to fit within the committee’s work period.
facts: Proposed safeguard
Set milestones for preservation, responses, enforcement review and reporting. Assign an owner and a fallback source for every critical request.
choices: lessons-contested
Assess delay one request at a time using the request, objection, court action and actual production dates.

lessons-contested.title: Contested requests
lessons-contested.summary: A dispute over presidential records reached the Supreme Court. On January 19, 2022 it denied a request to stay the mandate and enjoin disclosure pending review in Trump v. Thompson.
facts: Proposed safeguard
Record the scope, response date, asserted privilege and accommodation options. Counsel assesses enforcement separately from preserving an alternate source.
links: Supreme Court docket, Trump v. Thompson
choices: lessons-witnesses
Identify which objections concern witnesses and which concern records before choosing a response.

lessons-witnesses.title: Witness handling
lessons-witnesses.summary: The Select Committee reported that more than 30 witnesses invoked the Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination. Its final report discusses witness credibility and corroboration.
facts: Proposed safeguard
Keep a record of the testimony or asserted privilege, corroborating sources and access restrictions. An invocation alone does not establish the underlying allegation.
choices: lessons-referrals
Separate the corroborated findings that a committee can disclose from protected testimony and other restricted material.
witnesses
Use the distinct cooperation, immunity and clemency branches to evaluate lawful options.

lessons-referrals.title: Referrals
lessons-referrals.summary: The Select Committee referred possible federal offenses to the Department of Justice. Its report separately proposed legislative changes.
facts: Proposed safeguard
Record what was approved and sent. Track committee findings, legal referrals and receiving-office outcomes as separate entries.
choices: lessons-prosecutions
Check DOJ records and case dispositions separately from the committee’s referral record.

lessons-prosecutions.title: Prosecution outcomes
lessons-prosecutions.summary: On January 6, 2025 DOJ reported charging more than 1,500 people for crimes around the attack. Federal prosecutions produced convictions, including the linked trial example.
facts: What remains separate
The aggregate charging count does not establish the result for any particular person or theory. Case-specific judgments and dispositions answer that question.
Proposed safeguard
Use dated court records to track charges, convictions, dismissals, sentences and later clemency separately.
links: DOJ example of a trial conviction
choices: lessons-clemency
Check which federal proceedings and sentences the later proclamation addressed.

lessons-clemency.title: Clemency effects
lessons-clemency.summary: On January 20, 2025 the President commuted specified sentences, pardoned other covered convicted individuals and directed the attorney general to seek dismissal with prejudice of pending covered indictments.
facts: Proposed safeguard
Check federal clemency and court dispositions against the specific conduct and case. A state route requires genuinely independent state-law authority and facts supporting it.
choices: lessons-presidential-immunity
Analyze presidential immunity separately from clemency and state-law jurisdiction.
coordination-screen
Counsel may assess a possible state-law issue after identifying independently supportable facts.

lessons-presidential-immunity.title: Presidential immunity
lessons-presidential-immunity.summary: Trump v. United States distinguishes absolute criminal immunity for acts within exclusive constitutional authority, at least presumptive immunity for other official acts, and no immunity under that doctrine for unofficial acts.
facts: Proposed safeguard
Counsel assesses the conduct and applicable evidentiary and jurisdictional limits independently. The classification and outcome depend on the specific acts and applicable law.
links: Supreme Court opinion, Trump v. United States
choices: coordination-screen
Continue only if counsel identifies a separate state-law issue and can support the factual and legal basis for the next step.
